meta.title: Latin American politics knowledge network, c. 1950-2026
meta.description: Key works and debates in Latin American politics: democratization and transitions, bureaucratic authoritarianism and military and one-party rule, hybrid regimes and democratic erosion, presidentialism and executive-legislative relations, parties and party-system institutionalization, populism and the left turn, clientelism and vote buying, voters and partisanship, inequality, redistribution and social policy (including conditional cash transfers), development strategies (ISI, dependency, neoliberal reform and commodity booms), state capacity and historical legacies, subnational politics, decentralization and federalism, crime, violence and criminal governance, courts and judicial politics, corruption and accountability, indigenous and ethnic politics, social movements and labor, civil-military relations and transitional justice, and US-Latin American relations. Works shared with the other maps are imported from them; others are top-cited 2006-2026 articles selected via Crossref (Latin American studies and political science journals) and anchoring books and classics. Direction: source (later or dependent work) -> target (earlier or anchoring work).

edge_types.builds_on: source extends or relies on target's argument or evidence
edge_types.challenges: source contests target's claim, mechanism or evidence
edge_types.qualifies: source adds a scope condition or moderating factor to target
edge_types.extends_to_new_case: source applies target's logic to a new population, period or domain
edge_types.synthesizes: source integrates target with other work
edge_types.mechanism_tested_by: source tests a mechanism implied by target

meta.verification: Repo works come from the user's Zotero library. Works imported from the other maps keep their verification. Crossref-selected works take title, authors, year, venue and DOI from Crossref records. Anchors are checked in Crossref separately; see each node's `verified` field. One-line claims for non-repo works are my summaries.
